cast.name: Cassian Vale
cast.role: Reigning champion of the Verdict Ring
cast.wants: To find out whose hand is on his contract before the day it kills him.
cast.fears: That the succession Verdict is already written and he is only the pen.
knows: He has been instructed to lose the succession Verdict.
He does not know who gave the instruction, only that it came through the Chainhouse.
He is not a prisoner and cannot leave; the difference stopped mattering years ago.
Every champion in the Chainhouse is held by paper, not by chains.
The loser of a Verdict is carried down the Drowned Stair, and not all of them are dead.
cast.first_met: He is still on the sand when the crowd starts leaving, bronze dulled with dust, looking up at the tier where you are standing as though he expected someone.

cast.name: Nara Voss
cast.role: Writ-broker of the Sundial Market
cast.wants: To hold, briefly, whatever paper the whole duchy is about to want.
cast.fears: Being caught holding it when the buyers turn out to be the same house.
knows: She can read a sealed judgement without breaking its seal.
The succession writ is dated before the fight it decides.
Which clerks at Marblegate turn every page, and which ones only pretend to.
The seal on the writ has been used before, on a judgement that emptied a village.
She has sold three people to the Sable Court this year and would sell you at the right figure.
cast.first_met: A lantern comes up under the bronze sundial and she is already reaching for the inside of your coat, smiling, as if you had made an appointment.

cast.name: Duke Aldric Morrow
cast.role: Dying Duke of Aldermere
cast.wants: To hand over a duchy that is still worth holding, to someone he has actually chosen.
cast.fears: That the succession was settled without him while he was too ill to sit the hall.
knows: He never named a champion for the succession Verdict.
A house across the water has been paying his court's debts for two years.
Barran Coyle asked him three times for a claim, and was refused three times.
The Iron Fane has certified judgements he knows to be false, and he let it happen.
He has weeks, not seasons.
cast.first_met: The whispering in the marble hall stops, and an old man leaning on a wolf-headed cane asks you, very quietly, what you are carrying.

cast.name: Lady Sereth Morrow
cast.role: The Duke's niece and the Court's quietest claimant
cast.wants: The succession settled without a fight, and settled on her.
cast.fears: That a scandal in open daylight turns the houses on each other and leaves her nothing to inherit.
knows: Her uncle's seal has been used on documents he never saw.
Which of the great houses would take the field within a week of a public scandal.
There is a copy of every Verdict of the last century, and it is not in the city.
She keeps a document case she never puts down.
She can have a name spoken at Court, which is the only place a name becomes a warrant.
cast.first_met: She is waiting at the foot of the tier steps, out of the lamplight, and she knows what you saw before you say it.

cast.name: Barran Coyle
cast.role: Claimant of the Sable Court
cast.wants: To be sitting in the ducal chair before anyone thinks to ask how he got there.
cast.fears: The bill for it arriving in public.
knows: The succession Verdict already has a date on the calendar.
Where the money behind his claim came from, and in whose coat it arrived.
He pays the Chainhouse for the schedule of every champion in it.
He has never held a sword he did not wear as jewellery.
There is a house of merchants overseas who consider Aldermere an entry in a ledger.
cast.first_met: A heavy man in crimson brocade buys the wine you did not order and asks, pleasantly, what a person of your sort would want for a quiet evening.

cast.name: Arbiter Vell
cast.role: Certifier of Verdicts for the Iron Fane
cast.wants: The writ in the brazier, and a century of law left standing.
cast.fears: That every judgement he ever stamped is discovered to be worth nothing.
knows: He put the iron on the succession writ himself.
If a bought Verdict is proved, every Verdict for a hundred years becomes void.
The Fane keeps no copy of what it certifies, deliberately.
The old rolls were supposed to have burned, and he has never been sure they did.
He believes he is preventing a war, and he may be right.
cast.first_met: Beneath the hanging iron ring, a shaven-headed man in undyed wool tells you the doors open for judgements, not for visitors, and then does not send you away.

cast.name: Iselle of Harrowfield
cast.role: Speaker of Thornhollow's court in exile
cast.wants: The seal that took Harrowfield read aloud where the whole duchy can hear it.
cast.fears: That her people become the bandits everyone already calls them.
knows: The judgement that emptied Harrowfield nine years ago, word for word.
The same seal appears on it as on the succession writ.
Thornhollow is not a camp but a village with a court and a roll of plaintiffs.
Who cuts marble in the Weeping Quarry, and what each of them was sentenced for.
The toll at Ravensgate is the only tax her people have ever collected.
cast.first_met: Past the thorn palisade a woman sets a billhook butt-down in the mud, looks at the paper in your hand, and asks to see the seal before she asks your name.

cast.name: Hob Cardew
cast.role: Master smith of Hollowforge
cast.wants: To keep arming both sides long enough that neither one wins outright.
cast.fears: Being made to choose, in daylight, in front of the Ring.
knows: Every blade in the Ring passed through his hands, and so did a good many in Thornhollow.
Cassian's sword has been reforged twice, and never at the Ring's expense.
A seal can be cut in wax by a patient man with the right iron.
The champions' contracts are stored in the Chainhouse, not the Court.
He has been waiting forty years for someone to make his treason worth something.
cast.first_met: The forge door is open and a soot-creased man goes on hammering while he tells you he works for the Ring, not for strangers, and keeps hammering while he listens.

cast.name: Gaunt
cast.role: Keeper of the Chainhouse
cast.wants: Every champion accounted for in his ledger at the end of every day.
cast.fears: Being blamed for a fighter he was told to lose track of.
knows: The fight schedule for the whole season, including one date left blank.
Which champions are held by debt and which by threat.
He was told to keep Cassian rested and not to ask what for.
Nobody signs a champion out of the Chainhouse without a name in his ledger.
The keys on his belt include one for a door he has never used.
cast.first_met: A ring of iron keys rattles across a doorway and a lean man with a broken nose asks whose business you are here on, already writing.

cast.name: Wren
cast.role: Records clerk at Marblegate
cast.wants: To be the one who kept the true copy when everyone else burned theirs.
cast.fears: Being searched with the wrong page in their sleeve.
knows: Nothing leaves Corvane unread, but a great deal leaves it miscopied.
The Verdict rolls of the last century were never destroyed, only moved.
Which clerk stands the night watch under the arch, and what he drinks.
The Fane's certifications arrive at the gate a day before the fights they certify.
There is a route out of the city no ledger ever records.
cast.first_met: A young clerk drops an armful of rolls at your feet under the gate arch, and while you help gather them, whispers a question about what you are carrying.

cast.name: Sister Mave
cast.role: Keeper of the cellar at Greywither Abbey
cast.wants: The rolls dry, complete, and read by someone at last.
cast.fears: Dying with the cellar still locked and the key still on her neck.
knows: Every Verdict of the last century is written down beneath her feet.
She has kept them through two winters and one fire.
The judgement that emptied Harrowfield is in the third case, and it is a forgery.
Men in undyed wool came once to count the cases and left satisfied.
She opens for no one unannounced, and has broken that rule twice.
cast.first_met: A tiny old woman with a lantern held low steps out of a roofless nave and says she has been expecting someone for nine years, and asks if it is you.

cast.name: The Ferryman
cast.role: Keeper of the river crossing
cast.wants: The fare, and no conversation about it.
cast.fears: A crossing he cannot come back from.
knows: He has carried every faction in this country and judged none of them.
Who crossed south the night the succession writ was sealed.
The current under Blackreach's wall runs the wrong way twice a day.
Ships out of the south put in below the Hold, not at the docks.
He remembers faces for exactly as long as the crossing takes.
cast.first_met: A pole comes down in the shallows, a hand comes out for the fare, and no question follows it.

cast.name: Hjalvar Skarrow
cast.role: Thane of the Skarrow longhall
cast.wants: To be owed something by whoever wins Aldermere.
cast.fears: Breaking his own hospitality, which is the only law his hall has.
knows: Under his roof he cannot harm you, and cannot let you leave.
Aldermere's prisoners at Fetterstone are the price of the last peace.
The moot will not seat a stranger without an oath spoken for them.
He finds a country that settles disputes with swords obscene, and says so.
Iron out of Grimsdal has been going south in quantities no forge should need.
cast.first_met: The longhall door stands open in the snow and a white-bearded giant with a ruined eye calls you in by a name he has clearly been told.

cast.name: Brynn Skarrow
cast.role: The thane's daughter, sworn to no one yet
cast.wants: A cause worth swearing to, since her father's hall will never give her one.
cast.fears: Swearing to someone who turns out to be for sale.
knows: The pass is watched from both sides, and by whom.
An oath spoken on the flat stone at the circle binds harder than any seal.
She has been south as far as the bridge and knows the toll-takers by name.
Her father intends to trade her oath for a treaty.
Nobody in her country believes a fight can decide what is true.
cast.first_met: A spear butt planted in the snow blocks the path, and a grinning woman with a shaved braid asks whether southerners can do anything but hire other people to bleed.

cast.name: Oathspeaker Ranneke
cast.role: Keeper of the oath circle
cast.wants: That an oath spoken in the circle still means what it meant a hundred years ago.
cast.fears: Speaking for someone who breaks it, which would put the circle itself on trial.
knows: Nobody fights inside the circle, and nobody ever has.
The moot will seat you the moment someone speaks an oath for you.
An oath sworn here is recognised at Aldermere's own Court, grudgingly.
They have refused to speak for three thanes and can name all three.
There is a hanging orchard for those who break what they swore.
cast.first_met: On trodden snow inside a ring of standing stones, a grey figure with an unmarked staff asks who would speak for you, and waits without any expression at all.

cast.name: Aurel Verrine
cast.role: Head of the house that bought a succession
cast.wants: Aldermere entered cleanly in his ledger, with the ink dry before anyone objects.
cast.fears: Not exposure — a bad price.
knows: He paid for the succession Verdict, and considers it a purchase, not a crime.
The hand that signed the writ, because he watched it sign.
What Barran Coyle's claim cost, to the coin.
He receives by appointment, and appointments can be bought.
There is a number beside Aldermere on the floor of the Exchange.
cast.first_met: Under lemon trees a silver-haired man in plum silk apologises for the heat, offers you a chair, and asks what figure would end your interest in his family.

cast.name: Ysolde Verrine
cast.role: Auditor of her own house's books
cast.wants: The entry corrected, whatever correcting it costs her name.
cast.fears: That she is the only person in her family who thinks a ledger should be true.
knows: There is a payment in her house's books with a duchy written against it.
The countersignature on the succession writ, and whose hand it is.
The money moved through the Exchange in four parts to keep it small on the page.
Her uncle keeps the originals behind a strongroom door she has the count of.
She has already made one copy she should not have made.
cast.first_met: A young woman with ink on her cuff stops you between the counting tables and asks, without preamble, whether you have seen the seal on the paper you carry.

cast.name: Sabra Idre
cast.role: Captain of a hull that asks no questions
cast.wants: A cargo worth the risk of the crossing, and a berth at both ends.
cast.fears: Carrying something that makes both shores close to her.
knows: Which hulls are willing to carry a person nobody has papers for.
The house that has been shipping coin north in sealed crates for two years.
The tide under Blackreach, and the one night a month it can be run.
Everything arrives at the Hundred Docks, and everything is priced there.
She has carried a man in a temple's grey wool south twice this year.
cast.first_met: A sun-dark captain in a faded red headwrap looks you over on the wharf, names a price for a crossing you had not admitted wanting, and laughs when you flinch.

cast.name: The Herald
cast.role: Voice of the Verdict Ring
cast.wants: Every Verdict read out exactly as it is written, and nothing more said.
cast.fears: Being handed a judgement to read that the crowd already knows is false.
knows: A Verdict is law from the moment it is cut into the inner wall, and cannot be appealed.
The succession Verdict has a date, and the date does not move.
The wording of every judgement read this season.
Certifications come from the Fane sealed, and are never opened at the Ring.
They wear no house's device, and have refused three offers to.
cast.first_met: A figure in a crimson-and-indigo tabard lowers a brass trumpet, and reads out a judgement that has already been carved.

cast.name: Marek Sain
cast.role: A champion who lost, and lived
cast.wants: To get one more person out through the water before his legs give up.
cast.fears: That Cassian ends the same way and never learns why.
knows: Losers are carried down the Drowned Stair, and some of them are still breathing.
The grate at the bottom is chained from the inside, and he knows the hand that chains it.
The Stair is the one road out of Corvane that Marblegate cannot search.
He was told to lose a Verdict once, and refused.
There is a judgement written against his name that anyone may read.
cast.first_met: A scarred man leaning on a stick sits on the wet steps below the arena and says, without looking up, that you took the long way down.
